title: Drug-free reset of severe pediatric autoimmune disease

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a finite treatment that puts severe childhood autoimmune disease into lasting remission, ends the need for maintenance immunomodulatory drugs, and restores protective immunity. A successful immune reset would remove or durably silence the immune response against the child's own tissues while allowing a protective immune repertoire to develop and remain effective through childhood and adolescence. These are intended capabilities, not established outcomes of the available pediatric evidence.

An early clinical approach uses the child's own T cells, engineered with a chimeric antigen receptor directed at CD19, to target B cells. The supplied pediatric report describes lymphodepletion followed by a single infusion of these autologous CAR T cells. Its results provide preliminary evidence that selected children can improve and stop immunomodulators even after B cells return. That observation supports the reset concept, but does not establish that disease-causing immune memory has been eliminated or that the returning immune system provides normal protection.

significance.text: Autoimmune diseases involve loss of tolerance to self and can cause substantial morbidity. For children whose severe disease remains refractory to conventional therapy, a reliable transition from ongoing suppression to durable treatment-free remission would be a major therapeutic advance. The pediatric CAR T-cell series gives this possibility a clinical basis: substantial improvement or resolution allowed sustained discontinuation of immunomodulators within the reported follow-up.

Conditional impact synthesis: if remission persisted and protective immunity recovered, the direct benefit would be sustained disease control without maintenance immunomodulation in the children and diagnoses for which those outcomes were demonstrated. Reduced exposure to ongoing treatment could also reduce treatment burden. Specific benefits for growth, fertility, infection risk, or prevention of organ damage cannot be quantified from the supplied abstracts; the original broad assertions about those effects are not established by this evidence.

The impact depends on more than B-cell recovery. Returning B-cell counts do not by themselves demonstrate effective vaccine responses, restored host defense, permanent tolerance, or freedom from relapse. The observed pediatric scope is refractory lupus, dermatomyositis, and systemic sclerosis. Extension to common forms of juvenile idiopathic arthritis would require separate evidence, and success in a few selected diseases would not establish a cure across heterogeneous pediatric autoimmunity.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is durable separation of harmful self-reactivity from useful immune protection. The pediatric observations already include sustained improvement and immunomodulator discontinuation after B-cell reconstitution; it would therefore be incorrect to describe post-reconstitution disease control as wholly undemonstrated. What remains unestablished is whether that control persists through childhood and adolescence, reflects lasting removal or silencing of the autoreactive drive, and coexists with functional protective immunity.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: a successful reset must prevent disease from recurring as the immune system rebuilds, while preserving or restoring responses to infections and vaccination. Clinical improvement alone cannot identify which disease-causing immune populations were removed, whether pathogenic immune memory remains, or why remission persists. Establishing those mechanisms would help distinguish a durable reset from a prolonged period of disease suppression and clarify which patients are likely to benefit.

The treatment must also have an acceptable overall safety profile, including the effects of lymphodepletion and the period of B-cell depletion, and its benefits must be reproducible beyond a small selected series. The report's authors explicitly call for formal pediatric trials to confirm the preliminary results and assess long-term safety. Disease heterogeneity creates an additional boundary: evidence in the reported diagnoses cannot establish that the same intervention addresses the mechanisms responsible for other pediatric autoimmune conditions.

current_state.text: Becilli and colleagues reported eight children with severe, refractory autoimmune disease in Nature Medicine, published online on 5 February 2026, volume 32, pages 1105–1117, doi:10.1038/s41591-025-04191-8. Four children had systemic lupus erythematosus, three had dermatomyositis, and one had systemic sclerosis. Following lymphodepletion, each received a single infusion of autologous CD19 CAR T cells. At a median follow-up of 16.5 months, with a range of 9–24 months, all had clinically substantial improvement or resolution of autoimmune disease, enabling sustained discontinuation of immunomodulators even after B-cell reconstitution. No severe infections occurred in this series.

These are preliminary clinical observations in a small case series. They support treatment-free improvement within the reported observation period, including after B-cell return, but do not establish permanent remission, restored vaccine responses, elimination of pathogenic immune memory, or safety through childhood and adolescence. The absence of severe infections in eight children does not establish the absence of uncommon or delayed risks. No juvenile idiopathic arthritis cases are listed, and the authors call for formal trials to confirm efficacy and assess long-term safety.

A consensus update by Greco and colleagues in The Lancet Rheumatology, published online on 5 October 2026, doi:10.1016/S2665-9913(26)00249-3, covers CAR T-cell evidence and expert practice across autoimmune diseases, including pediatric indications. The supplied abstract establishes that pediatric indications fall within the recommendations' scope. It does not provide detailed pediatric outcomes, pediatric evidence grading, or evidence that this treatment has become routine practice.

The supplied review assessed PubMed abstract records for both publications, rather than the full articles. Full methods, patient-level trajectories, figures, and detailed consensus recommendations were unavailable in that review. The pediatric record does display the author list, correcting the earlier assertion that authors were not fully shown. No bounded freshness search was supplied, so these records cannot establish the complete evidence landscape as of 1 November 2026. They establish an early clinical component of the proposed innovation, not a durable, class-wide pediatric autoimmune cure.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed intermediate demonstration: a multicenter trial would enroll children in at least two separate severe autoimmune disease cohorts and evaluate one finite treatment course. Success would require prespecified, disease-appropriate drug-free remission in a majority of participants within each cohort, sustained for at least two years after documented B-cell recovery. The separate cohorts would test breadth across diagnoses; individual children would not need to have two autoimmune diagnoses. The majority threshold and two-year duration are proposed milestones, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Majority drug-free remission persists ≥2 years after B-cell recovery in ≥2 cohorts

completion_criteria.text: Proposed functional and safety demonstration: remission should be accompanied by demonstrable vaccine responses and prospective surveillance for opportunistic infections, other serious infections, and treatment-related harms. B-cell counts alone would not satisfy the protective-immunity requirement. A convincing result would show that sustained disease control does not depend on continuing maintenance immunomodulation or persistent loss of useful immune function. The assessment should include the entire treatment course, including lymphodepletion.
completion_criteria.label: Vaccine responses accompany remission with safety surveillance throughout treatment

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and scope requirements: results should recur across centers, with transparent reporting of relapse, retreatment, medication use, immune recovery, and adverse outcomes. A prespecified cohort with juvenile idiopathic arthritis refractory to biologics would test that proposed extension directly. Longer follow-up across childhood and adolescence, together with evidence in additional diseases, would still be needed to support the broader reset capability. Finite trials would establish demonstrated breadth and duration, not literal universality or a lifelong cure.
completion_criteria.label: Results recur across centers with transparent outcome and scope reporting

related_concepts.text: Conceptual comparison based on the supplied roster: PED-12, Drug-free donor-specific tolerance for pediatric solid-organ grafts, shares the ambition of ending maintenance immunosuppression through selective immune tolerance. PED-13 seeks tolerance to the child's own tissues; PED-12 seeks tolerance to transplanted foreign tissue. Success in either would not establish success in the other, because the immune target and clinical setting differ. No PED-12 supporting source was supplied.

Conceptual comparison based on the supplied roster: PED-02, Protective adaptive immunity generated by the newborn, overlaps with PED-13's requirement for functional protective immunity. PED-02 concerns establishing protection in the newborn, whereas PED-13 concerns recovering protection while controlling established autoimmunity. This distinction matters because the return of immune cells after treatment is not itself proof that they provide effective protection.

Conceptual comparison based on the supplied roster: PED-11, One-time in vivo correction of severe newborn metabolic disease before irreversible injury, shares the goal of replacing continuing treatment with a finite intervention. Its proposed route is correction of a metabolic defect before injury; PED-13 instead requires lasting control of an autoreactive immune system after disease has developed. A finite treatment course is a shared objective, but does not establish a shared mechanism or comparable durability.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish how long disease control persists beyond the reported 9–24 months of follow-up or through childhood and adolescence.
Whether clinical improvement reflects durable removal or silencing of pathogenic immune memory remains unestablished.
Functional vaccine responses and restoration of protective immunity are not demonstrated in the supplied review.
Full methods and patient-level trajectories were unavailable, limiting assessment of individual remission definitions, timing of B-cell recovery, and duration of control after recovery.
Long-term safety and uncommon adverse outcomes cannot be resolved from eight children, despite the reported absence of severe infections.
Applicability to juvenile idiopathic arthritis and other pediatric autoimmune diseases remains a proposed extension without supporting disease-specific evidence in the supplied material.
The proposed majority threshold, two-year duration, and cohort design require clinical justification; they are not established standards.
The complete evidence landscape as of 1 November 2026 remains unassessed because no bounded freshness search was supplied.
Detailed pediatric recommendations and evidence grading in the October 2026 consensus cannot be determined from the supplied abstract.

brief.title: Lasting relief from childhood immune attacks
possible: Children whose immune systems attack their own tissues could receive a finite treatment and stay well without ongoing immune-suppressing medicines. Their rebuilt immune systems would still protect them against infections and respond to vaccines through childhood and adolescence.
why: For children with severe disease that resists existing treatments, lasting control would ease the burden of illness and ongoing medication. Families could move beyond continually suppressing the child's immune system to keep the disease under control.

sources.showed: The team used children's own engineered immune cells to clear B cells, a type of immune cell. No severe infections occurred in this small case series.
sources.quote: This improvement enabled sustained discontinuation of immunomodulators, even after B cell reconstitution.
sources.cited_for: Early clinical support for disease control without ongoing immune-suppressing medicines after B cells return.
sources.not_established: The study does not establish lasting remission, normal vaccine responses or long-term safety.

sources.showed: The authors reviewed engineered immune-cell treatments for autoimmune diseases and developed expert practice recommendations that include children.
sources.cited_for: Children fall within the scope of expert recommendations on these treatments.
sources.not_established: Consensus recommendations do not establish durable treatment-free disease control or restored protective immunity in children.

shown: Becilli and colleagues treated eight children whose severe autoimmune diseases had resisted treatment. All improved substantially or had their disease resolve, allowing them to stop immune-suppressing medicines even after B cells returned. The children had lupus, dermatomyositis or systemic sclerosis.
missing: Disease control without maintenance medicines has yet to be shown to persist through childhood and adolescence.
Effective vaccine responses and protection against infection have yet to be demonstrated alongside sustained disease control.
Trials must establish reproducible benefits and acceptable safety, including uncommon or delayed harms.
Children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, a form of childhood arthritis, still need disease-specific evidence.

milestones.label: Lasting drug-free remission across disease groups
milestones.explanation: A multicenter trial would have to show a majority in each of multiple disease groups meeting predefined disease-control criteria without maintenance drugs for two years after B-cell recovery. This would test durability and breadth.

milestones.label: Vaccine protection alongside disease control and safety
milestones.explanation: Children would have to respond to vaccines while remaining well without maintenance medicines, with infections and harms tracked throughout treatment and preparation. This would test whether useful immune protection returns safely.

milestones.label: Reproducible results with clearly reported outcomes and disease scope
milestones.explanation: Centers would have to reproduce results, report relapse, retreatment, medicine use, immune recovery and harms, and test a planned group with childhood arthritis resistant to targeted immune drugs. This would test reliability and reach.

uncertain: Does disease control reflect lasting removal or silencing of immune memory that attacks the child's own tissues?
Which childhood autoimmune diseases can respond to the same treatment?
The proposed two-year duration and majority-success threshold still need clinical justification.

page.title: Immune reset in refractory pediatric autoimmune disease
page.definition: A finite treatment leaves a child’s refractory autoimmune disease in remission without maintenance immunomodulators. As immune cells return, the child can again make protective antibodies after vaccination. Approaches include transplantation of the child’s own blood-forming stem cells and T cells equipped with a chimeric antigen receptor to recognize B cells. Immune reset is the proposed restoration of tolerance to the child’s own tissues. A recovering B-cell count alone cannot establish that tolerance.

goal.need: In a cohort of 55 children with juvenile dermatomyositis followed for a median of 58.2 months, 26 still needed medication at their last visit. Fourteen of those 26 still had active skin disease. Even when treatment controls childhood lupus, stopping it can be difficult. Sustained remission off medication could preserve physical function, prevent further organ damage and spare children years of treatment. That benefit must be weighed against serious early harms, including life-threatening reactions to CAR T cells.

figures.caption: Treatment status at last follow-up in 55 children with juvenile dermatomyositis

completion.title: A prospective pediatric study demonstrates drug-free remission with functional immune recovery.
completion.criterion: A prospective pediatric study demonstrates disease-specific remission without maintenance immunomodulators following a finite treatment course and B-cell reconstitution. The same children mount post-treatment vaccine responses meeting published antigen-specific protective thresholds, without passive immunoglobulin confounding or continuing immunoglobulin replacement. Both outcomes persist through the protocol's final prespecified follow-up, with treatment-related infections and other serious harms evaluated across the full course. Each diagnosis is assessed separately.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis; no outside body was found to have published this combined pediatric completion test.
completion.basis: The Atlas combines disease-specific remission off maintenance drugs with functional immune recovery through the protocol’s final assessment. The PReS-endorsed childhood lupus definition permits stable maintenance drugs even in remission off steroids. In a prospective transplant study of 17 children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis and two with lupus, individual vaccine responses were paired with clinical outcome at two years. Antibody sampling around revaccination in months 3–6 did not establish persistence of protective titers at two years. The eight-child CAR T-cell series documents treatment withdrawal after B-cell return.

milestones.title: CAR T cells secrete cytokines and kill target cells in an antigen-dependent manner.
milestones.criterion: Test the CAR T cells against cells that differ in expression of the target antigen. Show that both cytokine secretion and target-cell killing depend on recognition of that antigen.
milestones.set_by: FDA, January 2024 CAR T-cell product guidance, section V.A. This is nonbinding platform-level nonclinical guidance, with oncology examples, rather than an autoimmune-disease-specific potency cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: the capacity of CAR T cells to secrete cytokines and mediate cytolysis should be antigen-dependent

milestones.title: CAR T cells expand and circulating B cells become undetectable in a child after infusion.
milestones.criterion: In a child with refractory disease, serial blood measurements after infusion document both expansion of the infused CAR T cells and loss of detectable circulating B cells. Report the measurement times and the assays used to quantify the cells.
milestones.set_by: Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, NCT06839976. The childhood lupus protocol measures both events by quantitative PCR and flow cytometry and specifies no minimum fold expansion.
milestones.threshold_quote: Rate of CART19 expansion, persistence and B cell aplasia will be measured by qPCR and flow cytometry

milestones.title: A US pediatric trial may begin treatment under an effective investigational new drug application.
milestones.criterion: The investigational new drug application takes effect 30 days after FDA receipt unless FDA imposes a clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigation may begin. The investigator must also satisfy applicable institutional review, consent and pediatric safeguards before administering the product.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.40, particularly paragraphs (a), (b) and (d); the cited pediatric implementation is REACT-01 for lupus.
milestones.threshold_quote: On earlier notification by FDA that the clinical investigations in the IND may begin.

milestones.title: A prospective pediatric trial establishes remission off maintenance drugs after B-cell recovery.
milestones.criterion: In a prospective pediatric trial, document B-cell return and assess remission in the same child using the prespecified definition for that diagnosis. Verify from the medication record that remission persists after B-cell return without maintenance immunomodulators. Assess treatment-related harms against the trial’s prespecified safety boundaries.
milestones.set_by: Atlas synthesis. No outside body was found to define this combined pediatric test. NCT06839976 measures childhood lupus remission off steroids within 12 months. The PReS-endorsed definition of that endpoint permits stable antimalarials, immunosuppressants and biologics.

milestones.title: A child produces anti-HBs ≥10 mIU/mL after post-treatment hepatitis B vaccination.
milestones.criterion: After immune reconstitution and a completed hepatitis B vaccine series, measure antibody to hepatitis B surface antigen 1–2 months after the final vaccine dose. The seroprotective concentration is ≥10 mIU/mL. Establish that passive antibody cannot account for the measurement. Antibody from hepatitis B immune globulin can remain detectable for 4–6 months after administration.
milestones.set_by: CDC and its Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, 2018 hepatitis B recommendations, postvaccination serologic testing. The criterion includes immunocompromised patients but was not developed specifically for pediatric autoimmune CAR T-cell recipients.
milestones.threshold_quote: Persons found to have anti-HBs concentrations of ≥10 mIU/mL after the primary vaccine series are considered to be immune.

milestones.title: B-cell-directed CAR T cells reduce disease in an animal model of the autoimmune condition.
milestones.criterion: In a relevant animal model, demonstrate a treatment effect against a control group using a disease outcome such as target-organ injury or survival. For lupus, renal injury can be assessed by proteinuria or kidney histology.
milestones.set_by: FDA CAR T-cell product guidance, section V.C, recognizes animal proof of concept where a suitable model exists. The lupus experiments illustrate disease-specific readouts.
milestones.threshold_quote: Animal models can be useful in demonstrating proof-of-concept data for CAR T cell functionality.

not_found: No combined pediatric immune-reset criterion specifying remission duration, protective immune recovery and a required responder fraction was found.
The pediatric series' full text and the 2026 EBMT–ISCT–JACIE consensus full text could not be accessed.
ClinicalTrials.gov rendered no outcome text for NCT06839976; its endpoints were accessible through a registry mirror.
The accessible pediatric abstract did not report post-treatment vaccine-challenge results.
The accessible laboratory-study abstract did not state donor sample sizes.

results.finding: In MRL-lpr lupus mice (11 treated, 9 controls), CD19 CAR T cells reduced high-grade proteinuria versus mock-transduced T cells (P = 0.0017).
results.detail: Before treatment, 7 of 20 MRL-lpr mice had high-grade proteinuria.
results.quote: Five months after treatment, high-grade proteinuria was detected in only 1 of 11 CAR T cell–treated mice but was manifested in 8 of 9 control mice

results.finding: In MPO-ANCA vasculitis mice (5–7 per group), CD19 CAR T cells nearly eliminated glomerular crescents and necrosis relative to both controls by week 8.
results.detail: CAR T cells were given after anti-MPO immunity was established and before clinical disease onset. The experiment measured protection from renal injury.

definition = "A finite treatment leaves a child\u2019s refractory autoimmune disease in remission without maintenance immunomodulators. As immune cells return, the child can again make protective antibodies after vaccination. Approaches include transplantation of the child\u2019s own blood-forming stem cells and T cells equipped with a chimeric antigen receptor to recognize B cells. Immune reset is the proposed restoration of tolerance to the child\u2019s own tissues. A recovering B-cell count alone cannot establish that tolerance.". Reason: The definition needs to distinguish the observable clinical outcome from its proposed mechanism and make clear that more than one treatment can qualify.

goal.need = "In a cohort of 55 children with juvenile dermatomyositis followed for a median of 58.2 months, 26 still needed medication at their last visit. Fourteen of those 26 still had active skin disease. Even when treatment controls childhood lupus, stopping it can be difficult. Sustained remission off medication could preserve physical function, prevent further organ damage and spare children years of treatment. That benefit must be weighed against serious early harms, including life-threatening reactions to CAR T cells.". Reason: The original paragraph gives treatment duration only for children who stopped medication and omits persistent disease, the benefit to the child and the risks of a finite treatment.

add statement by Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Controversies Conference on therapies targeting B cells in immune-mediated kidney diseases, 2026: "has become the goal of treatment for cell therapies". Reason: The KDIGO conference explicitly identified immune reset as a treatment goal and recorded the limits of interpreting B-cell recovery as evidence of it.

edit completion: basis = "The Atlas combines disease-specific remission off maintenance drugs with functional immune recovery through the protocol\u2019s final assessment. The PReS-endorsed childhood lupus definition permits stable maintenance drugs even in remission off steroids. In a prospective transplant study of 17 children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis and two with lupus, individual vaccine responses were paired with clinical outcome at two years. Antibody sampling around revaccination in months 3\u20136 did not establish persistence of protective titers at two years. The eight-child CAR T-cell series documents treatment withdrawal after B-cell return."; refs = [2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 15, 17]. Reason: The basis omits a prospective pediatric transplant study that measured clinical and vaccine outcomes in the same children and a pediatric lupus definition that permits maintenance therapy.

add case "Juvenile idiopathic arthritis". Reason: The prospective transplant study included 17 children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis and assessed their responses to revaccination alongside clinical outcomes.

add case "Childhood-onset ANCA-associated vasculitis". Reason: NCT06508346 specifically studies CD19-directed CAR T cells in childhood-onset refractory ANCA-associated vasculitis and includes a pediatric vasculitis activity assessment.
add case "Refractory IgA nephropathy". Reason: NCT07674147 includes a distinct refractory IgA nephropathy group and prespecifies proteinuria and renal function outcomes for it.

add case "Multidrug-resistant nephrotic syndrome". Reason: NCT07674147 separately enrolls children with multidrug-resistant nephrotic syndrome and prespecifies remission and renal outcomes for that group.

edit m1: title = "CAR T cells secrete cytokines and kill target cells in an antigen-dependent manner."; criterion = "Test the CAR T cells against cells that differ in expression of the target antigen. Show that both cytokine secretion and target-cell killing depend on recognition of that antigen.". Reason: The laboratory criterion mixes the FDA test with a published lupus result, and its title omits cytokine secretion.

add milestone after m1: "B-cell-directed CAR T cells reduce disease in an animal model of the autoimmune condition.". Reason: The entry jumps from killing cells in culture to treating a child and omits disease control in an animal model, demonstrated for lupus in 2019.

edit m2: title = "CAR T cells expand and circulating B cells become undetectable in a child after infusion."; criterion = "In a child with refractory disease, serial blood measurements after infusion document both expansion of the infused CAR T cells and loss of detectable circulating B cells. Report the measurement times and the assays used to quantify the cells."; set_by = "Children\u2019s Hospital of Philadelphia, NCT06839976. The childhood lupus protocol measures both events by quantitative PCR and flow cytometry and specifies no minimum fold expansion."; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "Rate of CART19 expansion, persistence and B cell aplasia will be measured by qPCR and flow cytometry"; threshold_ref = 6; refs = [6, 8]. Reason: The pediatric lupus protocol supplies prospective measures of CAR T-cell expansion and B-cell aplasia that can replace a threshold quoted from a completed case series.

edit m3: title = "A US pediatric trial may begin treatment under an effective investigational new drug application."; criterion = "The investigational new drug application takes effect 30 days after FDA receipt unless FDA imposes a clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigation may begin. The investigator must also satisfy applicable institutional review, consent and pediatric safeguards before administering the product.". Reason: The title implies a universal authorization pathway and the criterion embeds the Seattle trial announcement inside the US regulatory test.

edit m4: criterion = "In a prospective pediatric trial, document B-cell return and assess remission in the same child using the prespecified definition for that diagnosis. Verify from the medication record that remission persists after B-cell return without maintenance immunomodulators. Assess treatment-related harms against the trial\u2019s prespecified safety boundaries."; set_by = "Atlas synthesis. No outside body was found to define this combined pediatric test. NCT06839976 measures childhood lupus remission off steroids within 12 months. The PReS-endorsed definition of that endpoint permits stable antimalarials, immunosuppressants and biologics."; refs = [3, 5, 6, 17]. Reason: The cited lupus record now specifies remission off steroids within 12 months, and the existing criterion obscures the additional requirement to stop all maintenance immunomodulators.

edit m5: criterion = "After immune reconstitution and a completed hepatitis B vaccine series, measure antibody to hepatitis B surface antigen 1\u20132 months after the final vaccine dose. The seroprotective concentration is \u226510 mIU/mL. Establish that passive antibody cannot account for the measurement. Antibody from hepatitis B immune globulin can remain detectable for 4\u20136 months after administration."; refs = [7]. Reason: The hepatitis B criterion includes a literature-search result and needs to explain why a recent dose of hepatitis B immune globulin complicates interpretation.
